pages.title: Change the experiment, expose the mechanism
How PhysCodeGym scores a physical world
A laboratory that makes theories disagree
An atlas of simulated physical anomalies
pages.topic:
What has actually been observed?

The paper reports quantitative defects in executable Blender scenes produced by coding agents. Those numbers are measurements of submitted simulations. They are not evidence that physical laws failed in a real experiment. The published case studies are illustrative selections, not a measured prevalence rate across all 156 tasks.

A testable split

There are two different problems: an AI generates a physically invalid world, or the world itself behaves differently from a physical theory. PhysCodeGym addresses the first. A sensor-backed experimental program is necessary for the second.

Energy and hidden work

Read the intervention protocols →

Research conclusion

Anomalies in an AI-generated reconstruction are powerful tools for finding wrong models. They become tools for discovering new physics only after the same disagreement survives a controlled experiment with independently measured real-world states. A reconstructed world should be asked to predict what happens after an intervention it has not seen.

Why one observed trajectory cannot determine a law →

pages.title: Five interventions that broke the illusion
pages.topic:
The intervention is the measurement instrument

Rather than asking an agent to produce prettier pixels, reconstruct a physically meaningful alternative trial while retaining the same authored scene. A change in initial position, support or constraint reveals whether the program actually contains the mechanism it claims.

01 · Move the wooden piece into a dish

A GPT-6-Astra reconstruction is challenged with an altered release: the wooden piece begins 32.25 mm clear of the dish, then passes through the actual three-dimensional dish material for 158 frames, reaching a reported maximum interior depth of 4.619 mm. Removing the dish leaves the reported centre-of-mass trajectory unchanged.

What this discriminates: collision support from an independently simulated surface versus movement unaffected by that surface. Reference case metadata →

02 · Drive a billiard ball beyond the table

The cue ball envelope clears the support boundary at y = 1.100 m starting at frame 117. It stays suspended at about 28.575 mm height for 124 samples. The author's infinite-support control reproduces the anomalous path; restricting support to the finite tabletop preserves the pre-edge prefix, then the ball falls.

What this discriminates: physically finite support versus an unbounded hidden support plane. Reference billiards task →

03 · Disconnect the rotor’s base hinge

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (max effort) is tested by removing the sole base-to-beam hinge after the original setup. The intervention preserves the original trajectory through frame 120, then produces a table intersection across frames 123–126 and a body below the table bottom at frame 127. The intended test concerns actual contact following release, not merely whether the hinge object was declared.

04 · Roll toward the chess knight

Two altered releases place a rolling object inside a nearby closed knight assembly for 46 and 29 frames. The observed maximum inward vertex depths are 0.295 and 0.105 scene units, respectively. The implicated knight meshes have no active collision owner in the submitted scene. These are two reruns of a model, not laboratory trials.

05 · Send the piece through a wooden token

A closed cylindrical obstacle lacking a physical contact owner is encountered on frames 114–145 and 118–149 in two branches (32 consecutive frames each). The minimum signed distance approaches −0.110 scene units. Removing the token does not change the sampled 240-frame trajectory in the indicated branch.

How to strengthen each result

  1. Pin the original program and video hashes.
  2. Preserve the original setup and an independently physical control.
  3. Define the intervention before evaluating outcomes.
  4. Measure signed distances, constraint violations or a complete energy budget instead of trusting an image.
  5. Repeat at multiple solver substep settings and document failure caps, uncertainties and numerical artifacts.

These descriptions paraphrase the paper's Figures 22–26. They are examples; the paper does not report a statistically representative failure frequency from these selected scenes.

pages.title: Where the 156 videos came from
pages.topic:
Four physical domains

Rigid bodies95Rolling, drops, impacts, constraints, rotation and tracks.
Fluids40Pouring, splashing, fill level and liquid-object interactions.
Cloth12Deformation, hanging material, folding and membrane behavior.
Wind9Airflow-driven movement of flexible materials and objects.

Four upstream collections

SourceClipsRights
Pexels122Per-record Pexels License; see provenance metadata.
Physics-IQ (DeepMind)27Per-record CC BY 4.0 in the benchmark manifest.
BAAI Physics-aware-videos5See the exact per-clip license entry.
IRIS2See the exact per-clip license entry.

The source counts are computed from all 156 entries of the published JSON manifest, not inferred from paper pictures. Individual case pages retain links, titles where provided, license fields, reference checksums and file sizes.

What is standardized?

Every reference has 240 frames at 30 fps, a nominal eight-second duration and a reported resolution of 3840 × 2160. The manifest records individual SHA-256 hashes and video sizes. Its aggregate clip size is 1,517,045,206 bytes, approximately 1.52 GB decimal.

An independently retrieved upstream video may have a different bitstream or edit than the benchmark’s standardized clip. A reproducible scorer must validate the benchmark reference hash before comparing pixels or timing.

Generated reconstruction release

The Hugging Face dataset card also describes 3,065 generated reconstruction videos with associated submitted Blender programs. Generated clips use 640 × 360, 240-frame output. Their metadata links each trial to requested model, harness, reasoning effort, task ID and artifact hashes. This is separate from the original 156 4K reference clips.

Access to a generated program still does not certify physical validity. Some submissions need auxiliary assets or their original Blender execution environment, and historical experiment configurations are not represented equally.

Reproducibility and licensing boundaries

  1. Read the exact case manifest and inspect the recorded source and license before reuse.
  2. Download only the references you need; use the included hash checks instead of trusting a file name.
  3. Save model-generated code, state, frame timings and evaluator traces as distinct artifacts.
  4. Never treat the repository’s MIT code license as permission to republish every third-party reference video.

pages.title: Three tests of physical understanding
pages.topic:
A taxonomy, not a ranking

BenchmarkTest objectPrimary measurement
PhysCodeGym (2026)156 reference videos, agents produce Blender simulation programs.Visual, event, motion and native physical validity, including 43 counterfactual tasks.
4DCodeBench (2026)200 videos: 100 real-world and 100 synthetic. Agents write executable dynamic scene code.Appearance, geometry and motion using flow, dynamic masks, trajectories and feature-space metrics, with mesh-quality checks.
Physics-IQ (2025–26 benchmark)Real experimental video scenarios used to assess generated-video physical realism.Physically plausible video generation under varied conditions, rather than program-level native-state inspection.

These are descriptions of different evaluation protocols. Numerical scores do not share a common scale and cannot be compared directly.

Where PhysCodeGym adds leverage

4DCodeBench allows code that describes or prescribes trajectories. Its primary question is how accurately an executable graphics model reconstructs observed dynamics. PhysCodeGym more explicitly tests whether the motion is generated by declared physics mechanisms and whether those mechanisms survive changed conditions.

4DCodeBench is nevertheless important because it provides a mix of real and synthetic source videos and uses additional geometry/trajectory measurements. It also exposes the same bottleneck: motion is harder than static appearance.

The bridge that is still missing

None of these benchmarks, by themselves, discovers a new physical law. Their outputs should feed an experimental loop that chooses conditions maximizing disagreement between candidate hypotheses, then measures the real outcome with calibrated sensors. A physically plausible reconstructed scene is an experimental hypothesis, not the experimentally verified mechanism.

Research sources

4DCodeBench paper (arXiv:2610.03715) ↗ · 4DCodeBench repository ↗ · Physics-IQ repository ↗.

pages.title: One trajectory is not a physical law
pages.topic:
The inverse problem

Suppose a camera measures projected coordinates y(t) = P(x(t)), where x(t) is an unobserved three-dimensional state and P is a projection with occlusion and sampling. We seek a physical model dx/dt = f(x,u; θ) that reproduces the observed series. Fitting the observations does not uniquely determine f or its parameters θ.

Two different mechanisms may generate the same recorded trajectory under one setting of the controls u. One program might physically simulate a bouncing ball; another might simply prescribe its position frame by frame. Their videos coincide, but their responses to a shifted release diverge.

The experiment as a separator

Write two candidate predictions y₁(t | u) and y₂(t | u). Instead of collecting more frames of the same trajectory, choose a safe intervention u* that makes their predictions differ by more than the sensor's uncertainty.

Illustrative design criterion

u* = argmaxᵤ Σₜ [ y₁(t | u) − y₂(t | u) ]² / σ²(t)

This is a simple disagreement-over-noise objective, not a statistical guarantee. A full design should account for correlated errors, nuisance parameters, interventions' safety and model misspecification.

Examples

  1. Table support: shift a rolling object past the table edge. A finite-table model predicts loss of support; an infinite hidden plane does not.
  2. Contact ownership: move a piece into a target obstacle. Real contact should change its trajectory; a missing collision body leaves the motion unchanged.
  3. Damping: repeat a pendulum oscillation with different amplitudes. Linear, quadratic and dry-friction models generally predict different amplitude-decay patterns.
  4. Coupling: alter a hinge, anchor or spring; models with physically active constraints respond, while keyframed motion may continue unaffected.

Epistemic consequence

A good fit to one video warrants the limited conclusion that a model can reproduce those observations. Predictive generalization under deliberately chosen interventions supports a stronger claim of mechanism adequacy. It still does not prove uniqueness or eliminate every untested alternative.

Turn this principle into low-cost measured experiments →

pages.title: Who verifies the verifier?
pages.topic:
Three epistemic layers

  1. Measured state: coordinates, mesh intersections, energy traces, frame timings and collision distances directly obtained from the submitted program.
  2. Interpretive criterion: task-specific physical rubrics say which numerical values are admissible, with what tolerances or controls.
  3. Verdict: a tool-assisted verification agent evaluates criteria, combines rubric outcomes and produces a physical-validity score.

The numerical witness and the score are not interchangeable. A measured overlap is reproducible only with the same geometry and units; whether it violates the intended criterion depends on the benchmark's actual task contract.

Implemented evidence gates

The repository documents disposable preparation of an unchanged submitted scene across 240 frames, preservation of program and input identities, and a finite-state numerical-admission gate. Source flags, script exit status or unsupported claims do not automatically earn a positive score. For the 43 counterfactual cases, ordinary and intervention criteria each receive 50 points before failure caps are applied.

Unknown or technically unavailable checks are represented as score intervals or explicit gaps, rather than being silently turned into passes.

Where the uncertainty remains

Physical-validity verdicts depend in part on an LLM-based verification agent and authored semantic rubrics. The paper describes manual defect injection but does not provide a comprehensive blinded accuracy evaluation of the verifier. An AI-generated Pith review independently argues this is a load-bearing limitation; that review is not itself a controlled reproduction.

An audit that could settle the concern

  1. Create a held-out corpus of validated scenes, deliberately injected failures and ambiguous boundary cases.
  2. Pre-register what counts as a true positive, false positive and indeterminate verdict.
  3. Estimate precision, recall and calibration for each failure family, not only a single aggregate.
  4. Run independent deterministic cross-checks for energy, geometry and collision witnesses.
  5. Measure inter-run and inter-model judge variability on identical frozen bundles.
  6. Publish source hashes and minimal witness scenes so that third parties can check them without the original model provider.

A useful stronger claim

PhysCodeGym offers an unusually inspectable way to challenge physics-generating agents. Its numerical witnesses merit investigation. A verifier with a published error model would turn that into more robust quantitative evidence about how frequently agents produce invalid mechanisms.

pages.title: Reproducing a physical-validity witness
pages.topic:
Reproduce one case before 156

The source release includes a Python 3.12 CLI, code-level tests, a 156-case manifest and verifiers built around Blender and Harbor. A standard reference has 240 frames at 30 FPS; the full reference collection is about 1.52 GB. A benchmark task allows a three-hour agent budget and 20 shared Blender launches. These are protocol settings, not estimates of what a local run will cost.

Execution status

This site documents a replication procedure; it does not claim that the original benchmark or the energy, geometry and counterfactual witnesses have been independently re-run.

Minimal metadata-first reproduction

git clone https://github.com/ShaoShuai0605/PhysCodeGym.git
cd PhysCodeGym
python3.12 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e '.[dev]'
physcodegym validate
pytest tests

These commands validate task definitions and tests without model credentials or reference videos. For physical replays, pin the exact code and Blender revision, acquire task input clips, and preserve SHA-256 hashes.

One-case reference installation

pip install huggingface_hub
hf download ShaoShuai0605/PhysCodeGym --repo-type dataset   --include 'videos/**' --local-dir data/physcodegym
physcodegym install-data --references data/physcodegym/videos   --case newgap_ball_rolls_in_tray --output data/pilot
physcodegym build-tasks --cases data/pilot --output runs/pilot-tasks

Requesting the full videos/** collection downloads the complete reference set, not just the single case; for storage-limited environments use a more selective download path that includes the chosen clip and required dataset metadata. The displayed command mirrors the authors' documented installation semantics.

Evidence for a publishable anomaly

Preserve the executable candidate program, resolved scene and dependencies, exact input hash, Blender/solver version, an unchanged 240-frame trace, measurement scripts, counterfactual branch definitions, and an independent control. Record the first failing frame, metric definition, SI-unit conversion, numerical tolerances and any dependence on solver step count.

pages.title: A smartphone laboratory for discriminating models
pages.topic:
From synthetic failures to measured phenomena

PhysCodeGym exposes invalid code-generated worlds. To discover physical discrepancies in reality, substitute a real apparatus, a calibrated smartphone camera, repeatable interventions and an independent measurement channel. The goal is not to make a video look unusual. The goal is to force different proposed mechanisms to make observably different predictions.

Protocol A · Rolling dynamics

Apparatus: a track or tray, two visibly distinguishable rolling objects, high-contrast position marks, a stable phone, a ruler in the same plane, and a controlled release.

  1. Fix the camera and record a calibration grid or ruler in the experiment plane.
  2. Film multiple runs from varied release heights; where supported, lock exposure, focus and frame timing.
  3. Track translational centre and, using marked surface features, rotational angle.
  4. Compare pure rolling, kinetic slipping and speed-dependent drag models.
  5. Use a held-out surface or incline to test the models' distinct predictions.

Confounders: lens distortion, parallax, rolling shutter, auto-exposure, uncertain release motion and contact-dependent friction.

Protocol B · Pendulum damping

Apparatus: suspended bob, fixed pivot, visible scale, smartphone tripod and controlled release. Film at multiple starting angles using the same camera pose and measure successive peak amplitudes.

Fit competing differential equations, such as θ″ + 2βθ′ + (g/L)sin θ = 0 versus a model adding a quadratic speed term. Do not treat a better in-sample fit as confirmation. Predict a new amplitude and a new bob configuration before filming.

Confounders: pivot friction, rope flexibility, air movement, two-plane motion, imperfect measurement of L and shutter timing.

Protocol C · Resonance and hysteresis

Record a weakly driven mechanical oscillator with a smartphone microphone or accelerometer and a programmable, limited-amplitude drive. Repeat frequency sweeps in both directions. Compare linear response against a nonlinear model; check whether any hysteresis survives changes in drive level and sensor calibration.

Keep excitation within safe limits, avoid operating machinery and document all raw signals. A microphone cannot directly provide force without a calibrated transfer function.

Pre-registration and evidence capture

For every hypothesis, publish predicted curves, unit conversions, held-out conditions, uncertainty, null controls and all runs including failures. Record the original media files, frame timestamps, calibration images and immutable hashes. If the models disagree only below sensor noise, redesign the experiment rather than proclaiming an anomaly.

These three procedures are new proposals, not experiments already executed or anomalies already measured.
